name: registry_recover
description: Replay the transaction logs (.LOG1, .LOG2) a registry hive was copied with onto a COPY of it, and read the key and value records of the result. A hive that was in use when it was copied is dirty (its two sequence numbers differ) and its newest state is in its logs; regkv reads the hive as it is. The logs are the ones you name: nothing is looked for beside the hive. The original and the logs are only opened for reading; the copy, a receipt and the records are written under work/<your id>/registry_recover-<id>/ (in a job, under $OUT). The replay follows the two log layouts (Suhanov's registry format specification; libyal's REGF notes) and does not use regipy's apply_transaction_logs, which writes every entry whatever its sequence number. New format (HvLE, Windows 8.1 and later): an entry is applied only when its signature and its two Marvin32 hashes are right and its sequence number is the one the hive needs next; an entry older than the hive's state, an entry that does not follow, and the log from an entry whose hash is wrong are NOT applied and are listed under `unrecovered` with the hive ranges their pages would have written. An entry is also NOT applied, whatever its hashes, when it lists no page, declares a hive bins data size that is not a positive multiple of 4096 or is more than the hive file's own bins plus 64 MiB (and 4 GiB), names a page that is not whole 512-byte sectors or lists more pages than its bins have sectors; the reason is under `unrecovered` and the scan stops at it. At most 50,000 entries of a log are scanned (about 2 KB each in memory; 122 MB measured with 50,001 entries none of which could be applied, and a receipt of 17 MB); the rest of the log is named in the receipt (`logs[].trailing`: where it starts and how many bytes) and is unrecovered. A long list of page references is listed as hive ranges up to 20,000 per entry and 200,000 in all; the rest are counted and named by their place in the log (`page_references`), where the log has them whole. The tool's own clock (max_seconds) is looked at while the hive, the logs and the recovered copy are hashed, while the log is scanned, while the pages hash is checked and while the pages are written (a hash the limit stopped is not made: the receipt names it under `not_hashed`, with the bytes that were read, and the status is partial); when it is reached the replay stops, no recovered copy is left, the entries that would have been applied are listed as not applied and the status is partial. Old format (a DIRT vector and dirty sectors): applied as a whole only when the log's own sequence numbers agree with each other and with the hive's primary number. A clean hive is not replayed; a log entry newer than a clean hive is reported, not applied. The recovered copy differs from the original in the pages of the applied entries and in the fields of its base block that the receipt names: both sequence numbers, the hive bins data size and the checksum always, and, for a new-format log, the root cell offset and the last-written time (taken from the base block of the log that holds the last applied entry) and the flags (those of that entry) where they differ; a log whose own base block checksum is wrong is not believed for them and the status is partial. An old-format log changes the first four only. It is a derivative: cite the original, the logs and this tool's version beside it. Records are read with regipy (keys.jsonl: path, name, depth, raw last-write FILETIME and ISO UTC, subkey and value counts, then each value with its type, size and raw data; changes.jsonl: what differs from the original when a replay applied something) and counted again by libregf's regfexport when it is installed: `independent_reader` says whether the counts agree, and a disagreement makes the status partial. regfexport is held to a ceiling: address space of a gigabyte and four times the hive, and output of 64 MiB and 64 times the hive (a damaged 8 KB hive made it take 5.5 GB and print 8 GB); when it passes one, fails or does not finish in time it is stopped, `why_not_finished` says which, its counts are not compared, and the status is partial. Not done: no other state than the one the logs lead to (earlier states are other sources), no repair of a hive that is damaged beyond its logs, no interpretation of values. A key name, a value name or a value data size that is longer than the cell it was read from is not followed into the next cell (regipy would read on, and a withheld value's bytes could end up in a path): the record's name becomes `[name withheld: ...]` with the hive offset and the numbers and none of the bytes, a value under such a name or such a key is withheld like a secret, a data size is cut at its cell, and each is a problem line (`records.problems`) that makes the status partial. SENSITIVE and withheld by shape: the V and SupplementalCredentials values of each SAM user, the values under the LSA secrets and cached-logon keys of a SECURITY hive, and any value whose name says password, secret, token or credential (a DWORD or QWORD excepted) are written as a record with their place, name, type and length, and not their bytes. `write_values: true` writes those values to values.jsonl with mode 0600 and is refused unless the tool runs as a job with secret_output: true; nothing is made when it is refused. A secret inside a value that does not look like one (a command line with a password in it) is not recognised and is written with the rest, so run the tool as a job with secret_output: true when the hive's content matters. Every answer carries status (complete, partial, failed) and status_basis; partial names what was not read or not applied. A hive larger than 4 GiB, a pipe or a device is not opened. Memory: the replay works in 1 MiB pieces and holds no page reference (about 50 MB resident for a 64 MiB hive and a 60 MB log, plus about 2 KB for each log entry scanned); reading the records is regipy's, which holds the whole hive in memory, so a 300 MiB hive was read at about 400 MB resident, and a hive or recovered copy over 512 MiB is replayed and not read (records.status skipped, with the reason, and the status partial). export: false skips the reading. It starts no program in a group of its own and ends regfexport with itself. regfexport prints its counts on a pipe: a process it leaves holding that pipe open is ended after one second, and the counts are then not trusted and not compared (independent_reader.regfexport.finished false, why_not_finished). The recovered copy and the records are written by this tool, not by a program, so a host that cannot adopt orphans does not change the status. INLINE PAGES ARE BOUNDED BY BYTES as well as rows: keys_inline and records.changes.inline each hold at most `limit` rows and 128 KiB, and a row over 4 KiB is shown by its small fields with inline_omitted (its size and its line in the file); records.keys_page and records.changes.page give total, returned, cut_by (rows or bytes) and next (the file and the line to read on from); a text of a problem or a list in the answer is cut at 2,000 characters, and an answer still over 768 KiB is printed without its inline pages (inline_dropped). Every row is whole in keys.jsonl and changes.jsonl, and the receipt carries the same bounded pages. VALUE COUNTS: values_declared_by_keys is the sum of what the keys declare and values_not_yielded_by_regipy what the library did not give (it skips a value of registry type 0x00200000 and ends a key's list at a value record it cannot parse, in both cases without an error): each such key is a problem line, those values are not in keys.jsonl and the status is partial; when regfexport's count equals the declared one, independent_reader.regfexport.difference_explained is true and status_basis says the difference is exactly those values. Measured on a real 12 MB SYSTEM hive with its logs: 69,989 of the 70,010 values regfexport had counted are read (the 21 others are of type 0x00200000) and the answer is 134 KB, where the version before read 184 values and printed 144.8 MB. INLINE VALUES: a value whose data is inside its record (four bytes at most) is read from the record for every registry type. regipy 6.3.0 reads up to 2 GiB of the hive file for such a value and returns that for a type it has no branch for (a device property under a Properties key, REG_LINK, REG_FILETIME, an unknown type), so one such value came back as megabytes of the hive; this tool replaces that read. BIG DATA AND REG_MULTI_SZ: the values of a key are read by this tool from regipy's copy of the hive, with regipy 6.3.0's records, names, types and decoding, and a value of more than 16,344 bytes that is kept in segments (a db record) is checked before its data is put together: one that declares more data than the hive file holds past its base block, whose list holds fewer segments than its size needs, runs past the end of the file or names one segment more than once, or one of whose segments lies past the end of the file, is not read; it is named under problems by its place in the key's value list and its type, and the answer is partial (regipy put together whatever the list named: one 16 KB segment named 160 times was a 2.5 MiB value, and a 548 KB hive declared one of 2 GiB). Every value's data counts against the walk's data budget (four times the hive's size) before it is read. A value that declares more than 16 MiB of data is not read: it is named under problems with the length it declares. The values of a key are handed out one at a time and stop at 64 MiB of data for the key, said under problems. A subkey list keeps each key the first time it names it, and is read no further after 4,096 elements in a row that name keys it already named, or past about 190,000 distinct keys (256 MiB of memory), each said under problems; a subkey list begun after the time limit is read to 16,384 elements and a value list to 4,096, and what is left is said. The hive is opened only when its base block and first bin are what regipy's open reads (the regf signature, a first bin of a positive multiple of 4096 bytes, the root cell the base block names inside the bins, allocated and a key, and the first allocated cell of the first bin that same cell): any other file is a failure that says what was found (regipy read a first bin of free space four bytes at a time, with no clock: a 40 MB hive took 58 s). A log's entries are used up to the first one whose pages hash (hash-1) is wrong, as Windows reads a log: none after it is applied, whatever its sequence number. A sequence number after 0xFFFFFFFF is 0. The keys, changes and values files, like the recovered copy, are results only with the receipt: a run stopped or refused before it removes them. A REG_MULTI_SZ is split by this tool in one pass and gives the strings regipy gives (empty ones left out); the bytes after its last NUL, and a string that is not valid UTF-16 with the rest of the data after it, are not in the answer, as with regipy, and are said under problems with their length (regipy dropped them without a word, and took 50 s on 2 MiB with no NUL). The tool's deadline is read before every value and every 256 subkey elements of a list begun before it: the values or subkeys of a key that were not read in time are said under problems. A value this tool refused or did not reach is counted under records.values_not_read_by_bounds and is not counted as a value regipy did not give (records.values_not_yielded_by_regipy). Stopped by SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, the tool answers with status failed and interrupted true (a stop is not a status), and no result it made is left.

hive.description: The registry hive file (a copy of it). It is only opened for reading

log1.description: The .LOG1 transaction log of that hive (named; none is looked for)

log2.description: The .LOG2 transaction log of that hive

export.description: Write keys.jsonl (and changes.jsonl when a replay applied something) (default true). false replays and writes the receipt only

write_values.description: Write the values that are withheld to values.jsonl under $OUT, mode 0600 (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job with secret_output: true; the answer never carries a value

limit.description: Rows of keys.jsonl shown inline (default 200, an inline page size); every row is kept, and the whole result is in the file the answer names

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds, 1 to 110 (default 90); a read that reaches it stops, says so and is partial
